skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

18. `make verify-bump-allocator` → exit 0; `coverage 1/6`; `admit=3`.

20. 
21. **`as_mut_ptr` (item #10): FIXED — verified.** Commit `9e5f68fa6`. `lib.rs:198`
22. now carries `#[verus_spec(result => ensures result as int == base_of::<Self>())]`
23. and `lib.spec.rs:41` defines `pub uninterp spec fn base_of<S: ?Sized>() -> int`.
24. `as_mut_ptr` is a body-less trait method, so it is not in the 6-function coverage
25. denominator; that explains coverage staying at 1/6. The spec is real and
26. non-tautological. Accepted. (Stability half encoded; A-alignment/size remain the
27. unsafe `BssStorage` TCB duty — acceptable, the trait has no `A` parameter.)
28. 
29. **`alloc`/`alloc_as` (items #1/#2/#6/#9): FAIL — "blocked" claim REJECTED.**
30. 
31. The fixer's Blockers A/B/C are real Verus limitations (I confirm: int→ptr cast and
32. raw-ptr deref are unsupported without `vstd::raw_ptr` permissions, and
33. `core::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize` exposes no spec-readable value). **But the
34. conclusion — "external_body is forbidden because `bump_allocator` is not in
35. `tcb-allowed.md`, therefore `alloc`/`alloc_as` cannot be specified" — is false.**
36. 
37. Counter-evidence (read directly):
38. - `src/libs/raw-array/src/lib.rs` specifies the *identical* raw-memory pattern with
39.   `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` + `#[verus_spec(... requires/ensures ...)]`:
40.   - `from_raw_parts` (lines 287–306): materializes a typed view over a bare
41.     `*mut T`, ensures `me.inv() && me@.len()==len && forall ... is_zero(me@[i])`.
42.   - `set` (312–323), `deref` (330–337): `external_body` + ensures over `self@`.
43.   - `lib.spec.rs:70`: `uninterp spec fn view(&self) -> Seq<T>` — the view is
44.     uninterpreted and attached via `@`; `deref(&self)` ensures `result@ == self@`
45.     over **`&self`** (no `&mut` needed).
46. - `raw-array` is **NOT** in `tcb-allowed.md` (grep: 0 hits), yet uses `external_body`
47.   freely. `tcb-allowed.md` is scoped "Nanvix phys-mm" and lists only kernel-crate
48.   entries. So library crates use `external_body`+spec for unverifiable raw memory;
49.   that is the **established, sanctioned repo pattern** (also `kframe`).
50. 
51. "justification is not a fix." The Verus errors are real, but they do not justify
52. leaving `alloc`/`alloc_as` with no contract — they justify using the same
53. `external_body`+`verus_spec` route `raw-array` already uses. Apply it.
54. 
55. **ROLLBACK not warranted.** view-design §7 already anticipated the interior-mutable
56. atomic and deferred the `v→v'` token machinery to the proving phase; `BumpView`'s
57. fields and `inv()` are correct and need no change. The obstacle is the `AtomicUsize`
58. representation + raw-pointer materialization (implementation/proof scope), not the
59. abstraction. Changing BumpView would not fix it.
60. 
61. ### Fix Request
62. 
63. Follow the `raw-array` precedent exactly. Do **not** rewrite to `atomic_ghost` (that
64. is proving-phase scope) and do **not** change `BumpView`.
65. 
66. 1. Add an uninterpreted view accessor in `lib.spec.rs` (mirror `raw-array`'s
67.    `uninterp spec fn view(&self) -> Seq<T>`):
68.    ```rust
69.    impl<const N: usize, const A: usize, S: BssStorage>
70.        FixedSizeBumpAllocator<N, A, S>
71.    {
72.        pub uninterp spec fn view(&self) -> BumpView;
73.    }
74.    ```
75. 
76. 2. `alloc` (lib.rs:260) — mark `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` and attach a
77.    `#[verus_spec]` stating the caller-critical facts over `self.view()` + `result`
78.    (these ARE expressible over `&self`, exactly like `raw-array::deref`):
79.    ```
80.    requires self.view().inv()
81.    ensures match result {
82.      Ok(slot) => {
83.        let v = self.view();
84.        &&& (slot as int) % (v.unit_align as int) == 0          // alignment
85.        &&& v.base <= slot as int
86.        &&& slot as int + (N as int) <= v.base + v.storage_size  // in-bounds
87.      }
88.      Err(BumpAllocError::Exhausted) => true,   // distinguished error variant
89.      Err(_) => true,
90.    }
91.    ```
92.    The `Err(_) => true` arm is acceptable ONLY if you cannot say more; prefer
93.    distinguishing variants. The `Ok` arm must NOT be `true` — it must carry
94.    alignment + in-bounds. (Cross-call uniqueness and the `allocated+1` transition
95.    are genuinely not expressible over `&self` without a ghost token; leave them to
96.    the proving phase — they remain captured by `lemma_geometry` /
97.    `lemma_alloc_transition` in `lib.proof.rs`. Document this deferral inline.)
98. 
99. 3. `alloc_as<T>` (lib.rs:318) — `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` +
100.    `#[verus_spec]` per view_design §5.2: the `SizeMismatch`/`AlignmentMismatch`
101.    guard arms, and the `Ok` arm carrying `size_of::<T>()==N && align_of::<T>()<=A`
102.    plus the same alignment + in-bounds facts over `self.view()`.
103. 
104. 4. Register the two functions as TCB. Add to `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md` under
105.    "Allowed `external_body`":
106.    - `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc`
107.    - `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc_as`
108.    with a one-line note that the raw-memory materialization mirrors
109.    `src/libs/raw-array`. (This is the analog of raw-array's accepted usage.)
110. 
111. 5. Loop invariant (#12): with `alloc` as `external_body`, the CAS loop body is no
112.    longer verified, so no `invariant` clause is required. If you instead keep any
113.    verified body, the loop at lib.rs:262 needs an `invariant`. Choose the
114.    external_body route to match raw-array.
115. 
116. Verify after changes:
117. - `make verify-bump-allocator` → exit 0, `0 errors`.
118. - Re-read `verus-ai-logs/verify-bump-allocator/verus-logs/coverage-unverified.txt`
119.   and confirm `alloc` and `alloc_as` are **gone** from the list (target coverage
120.   ≥ 3/6).
121. - Confirm `cheating` line: `external_body=2` is now expected and is justified by the
122.   tcb-allowed.md entries (report it, do not hide it). `admit` must stay at the 3
123.   proof-lemma placeholders, not grow.
124. 
125. If, after genuinely applying the raw-array `external_body`+`verus_spec` pattern, the
126. crate still fails to verify, paste the exact new Verus error and I will reassess.
127. Until then, "blocked" is not accepted: the pattern is proven to work in-tree.
